1319.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. No one has found the end of Ram, the all-pervading Ram. (O God,) we are your children, nurtured by you; you are the great Being, my father and my mother. The Lord's Names are countless and beyond reach; beyond reach, beyond reach is the Lord, the King. The virtuous and the wise have reflected much, (yet none has) found (his) worth, not even a jot. (Beings) ever sing the praises of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), of Gobind, but have not found the end of Gobind's praises. You are beyond measure, beyond weighing, beyond the beyond, O Master; though one repeat (your Name) much, your depth is not found. Your servants praise you, O Madho; they sing (your) praises, O Lord, O King. You are the ocean of water, and we are your fish; nowhere has your end been found. Show mercy to (your) servant, O Madhusudan; O Lord, grant (me) the repeating of the Naam. For me, a blind fool, the Naam is the prop; servant Nanak has found (it) through the Guru. ॥4॥
Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God. Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1319.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's servant, singing (his) praises, blossoms with joy. Through the Guru's teaching, devotion to the Lord, Har Har, has come to grace his mind; God wrote (this) on (his) forehead from the very beginning. Day and night I remember the Guru's feet; in my mind the Lord, Har Har Har, has come to dwell. In the world the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har, is the excellent thing; as sandalwood rubbed (gives its fragrance, so the Lord's) glory, rubbed (into the heart, spreads its scent). The Lord's servants have fixed their attention on the Lord, Har Har Har; all the Saakats go after them (in envy). The slanderer goes his way as his past deeds have ordained; (his) foot touches the she-serpent, and he is burnt (by her venom). O Lord, my Master, you are the protector of your servants; in every age you have protected your servants. What came of it that the demon was envious (of the devotee)? Doing all that, he himself withered and fell. All the beings and creatures that God has made are seized in the mouth of death. The Lord God, Har Har Har, has protected his servants; servant Nanak has come to his refuge. ॥4॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
The demon: the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu), who tormented his son Prahlad for his devotion to God; Prahlad held to his devotion.
1319.3: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat the Name of Jagannath, the Lord of the world. Whoever has meditated on the Lord's Name through the Guru's teaching, all his sins and sorrows have gone. (O God,) one tongue cannot sing (your) glory; make (me) with many, many tongues. Again and again, every moment and every instant, all sing (your) praises, yet they cannot tell your virtues, O God. Great love has taken hold of me, O God, my Master; I long to see God. You are the great Giver of all beings; you alone know our pain. If someone shows (me) the road, the path of God, tell me, what (shall I) give to such a one? All my body and mind I would offer, dedicate and hand over, if someone who has met God would unite (me with him). The Lord's virtues are many, many, very many, and great is (his) glory; we can tell only a very little. Our understanding is in your power, O God, the all-powerful God of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
1320.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat the praises of the Lord, of whom we hear that he is beyond telling. Dharam, arth, kaam and mokh, all of it follows behind the Lord's servant. That servant of the Lord meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on whose forehead is great fortune. Where God asks for the account in his court, there one is set free by having meditated on the Naam. Our faults of birth after birth are many; pain and the filth of Haumai (ego) cling (to us). The Guru, showing mercy, bathed (us) in the water of the Lord('s Name), and all sins and wrongs went away. In the hearts of his servants dwells God the Master; his servants repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Where the last moment comes, there the Naam, (our) companion, protects. Your servants sing your glory, O Lord, Har Har; O God, Lord of the world, they have repeated (your Name), O Lord. O God, Master, protector of servant Nanak, save us, sinking like stone. ॥4॥
The four padaarath: dharam (righteousness), arth (wealth), kaam (fulfilment of desire) and mokh (liberation), held to be the four aims of life.
1320.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord God knows what we think within. If anyone else slanders the Lord's servant, God does not heed a jot of what he says. Leaving all else, serve the Imperishable, who is the Master, God, higher than all. Through serving the Lord, death cannot (so much as) look at (his servant); it comes and falls at the feet of the Lord's servant. Whomever my Master saves, he gives good counsel, (as if) into his ear. One whose devotion my God accepts, no one can equal him. Behold the Lord's wondrous plays, O servant (of God): in the blink of an eye he knows the false from the true. Therefore his servant is in bliss: the pure in heart meet (him), and the false repent. O Lord, you are the Giver, the all-powerful Master; O Lord, I beg one gift from you. O Lord, show mercy and give servant Nanak (this): may your feet, O Lord, ever dwell in my heart. ॥4॥
1321.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O God, treasure of mercy, show mercy, (and) we shall sing the praises of the Lord. O God, I ever hope in you: when will you take me into your embrace? We are children, foolish and ignorant; the Father will teach (us) understanding. The son errs and spoils things moment by moment, (yet the children) will still be dear to the Father of the world. Whatever you give, O Lord, O Master, that alone shall we receive. For me there is no other place to which we might go. The devotees who are dear to the Lord, to them the Lord will be dear. Merging (their) light in the Light, they will blend into the Light. The Lord himself, becoming merciful, will himself attune (them) to himself. Servant Nanak is in (the Lord's) refuge, at (his) door; the Lord will keep (his) honour.
Chhaka 1: the first set of six shabads; the count is written after the shabad's numbers.
1321.2: Raag Kalyan Bhopali, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Narayan, O Master, you are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), the Supreme God, the remover of pain. O ocean of peace, O carrier across the world-ocean, O Lord, O Chintamani, all the devotees beg (at your door). O merciful to the meek, O Lord of the world, O Damodar, O Lord who knows every heart, O Gobind, O Murari, O Lord Mukand, those who have meditated on Sri Ram through the Guru's teaching have become free of fear. Those who have sought refuge at the feet of the Lord of the world, those servants have crossed the world-ocean. The Lord keeps the honour of his devotees; O servant Nanak, the Lord himself shows mercy. ॥2॥
Chintamani: the jewel that, by tradition, grants whatever is wished for in the mind.

Damodar (he whose waist was bound with a cord: the child Krishna), Murari (the foe of the demon Mur) and Mukand (the giver of liberation) are names of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; in Gurbani they are names of the one God.
1321.3: Raag Kalyan, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O God,) grant me this grace: as the bee (delights) in the nectar (of the flower), may (my) mind delight again and again in (your) lotus feet. I have no concern with any other water; O Lord, give (this) chatrik the drop (of your Name). Without meeting (you) there is no contentment; Nanak lives by beholding (your) sight. Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The beggar begs, and begs again, for the Naam alone, O Support of all, Master of all, Giver of every comfort. Countless people beg every kind of gift (at your door); whatever the heart longs for, that is received. Fruitful, fruitful, fruitful is (his) sight, O brother; touching (his feet) again and again, let us sing (his) praises. O Nanak, (so) the essence merges with the Essence, and the diamond (of the mind) is pierced by the Diamond (of the Lord). ॥2॥
The chatrik (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water, and to cry out for it.
1322.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The glory of my Beloved: that glory is ever new, and dyes the mind (with love). Brahma, Mahesh, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra beg (of him) the gift of devotion and (his) praise. Yogis, the wise, those deep in meditation and Sheshnag, all repeat (the Name of) the Lord of countless waves (of wonder). Says Nanak: I am a sacrifice to the Sants who are ever the companions of God. ॥2॥
The Siddhas are yogis held to have reached perfection; siddhi is attainment, the miraculous powers among it.
Sheshnag: the thousand-headed serpent of the Puranas, held to utter a new Name of God with every tongue.
1322.2: Raag Kalyan, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Through the love you give, O Lord, Har Har, through (your) love, with the eyes (you are seen), with speech (you are praised), with the ears (your praise) is heard; in every limb and in the breath there is peace. Here and there, in all ten directions, he pervades, alike in Mount Meru and in a blade of grass. Wherever one looks, there the Lord is seen, the Being, the Master (of all), the foremost. In the Saadh Sangat doubts and fears are wiped away, O Nanak, by speaking the knowledge of God. ॥2॥
1322.3: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God's) praises are (their) naad, the strain of bliss (their) Vedas; the sages, meeting in the circle of the Sants, speak and hear (them). (There is) wisdom, meditation, honour and giving; minds that relish (it) repeat the Naam with the tongue, and there sins are destroyed. Of those who know the way of union, the food of wisdom and the essence of attention on the Shabad, the japa and tapa go on unbroken. O Nanak, merged with (God's) Light like warp and weft, no pain punishes (them). ॥2॥
1322.4: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). What is the way to him? What shall I do? (Some) hold to meditation, the knowers of the Shastras to (their) knowledge; (but) how am I to bear this state of mine, which is beyond bearing? Vishnu, Mahesh, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra: at whose door shall I seek refuge? With one is a kingdom, with another heaven; (but) among millions, (with whom) can I say liberation is found? Says Nanak: the relish of the Naam is found if I hold to the feet of the Saadh. ॥2॥
1322.5: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Lord of (my) life, merciful Being, God, (my) friend, O Lord, destroyer of birth from the womb, of strife, of the net of death and of pain, O protector: I have held fast to the Naam, (and come) to your refuge; merciful God, (you are) my support. The helpless and the meek place (their) hope (in you); the Naam, O Master, is the mantra of (their) minds. Without you, O God, I know nothing (else); in every age you are the one I know. May the Lord dwell in (my) mind night and day; O Gobind, (you are) Nanak's support. ॥4॥
1322.6: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let us repeat (the Name of) God with mind and body. (On whom) the perfect Guru is well pleased, (theirs is) ever peace and bliss. Singing the praises of Gopal, all tasks have been fulfilled; (whoever) has remembered God, joining the Saadh Sangat, the pains of death have fled (from him). O my God, be merciful, so that day and night I may serve (you). Servant Nanak has come to (your) refuge, O Lord, O Being, O perfect Divine One. ॥2॥
1323.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My God knows every heart; he knows (all). Show mercy, O perfect Supreme God; (grant me) the unchanging, true Shabad, (the) mark (of entry to your door). (O God,) apart from the Lord no other is all-powerful; my hope is in you, your strength is in (my) mind. O Master, Giver to all hearts, what you give, that (we) wear and eat. Understanding, wisdom, skill, glory, beauty, colour, wealth, honour, all comforts and bliss (lie in the Naam); O Nanak, repeat the Name of Ram, (it is) every good. ॥2॥
1323.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The refuge of the Lord's feet brings every good; God's Name purifies the fallen. Whoever repeats (the Naam) without fear in the Saadh Sangat, Jamkaal (death) does not devour him. Liberation, the ways (to it) and countless comforts do not equal devotion to the Lord. O servant Nanak, one who longs for the sight of God does not wander into births again. ॥2॥
1323.3: Raag Kalyan, Ashtapadis, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Hearing (the Name of) Ram, the all-pervading Ram, the mind is drenched (with love). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), a sweet essence; through the Guru's teaching it is drunk in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise). As fire is in wood, and is drawn out by rubbing it with skill, (so) the Name of Ram is the light in all (creation); this essence is drawn out through the Guru's teaching. (The body) has nine doors, and all nine doors are tasteless; the Amrit essence trickles in through the Tenth. O Beloved, show mercy, mercy, mercy, (that) the Lord's essence may be drunk through the Guru's Shabad. The body is a town, a fine town; in it let the trade in the Lord's essence be done. (This essence is) jewels and rubies, priceless, beyond price; they are gained by serving the True Guru. The True Guru is the Master, beyond reach, beyond reach, a brimming ocean; let devotion (to him) be offered. (O God,) show mercy, show mercy: we are meek chatriks; put a single drop of the Naam into (our) mouths. The Beloved is the deep red, red dye; O Guru, give (me this dye) to dye (my) mind. Those dyed in the love of Ram, Ram, Ram, savouring the essence, drink it ever in deep draughts. (There is) the earth with its seven continents and the seas; (if they were) dug and the gold drawn out and set (before them), the servants of my Master would not desire these; they beg for the Lord alone: give (us) the Lord's essence. Saakat men, mortal beings, are ever hungry; they ever cry hunger, hunger. Running and racing, they run in the love of Maya, and cover distances of hundreds of thousands of kos. Exalted are the servants of the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har; what likeness can be given them? There is no likeness equal to the Name of Ram; (O God,) show mercy to servant Nanak. ॥8॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.
The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
1324.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, the Guru is the paaras; grant (me) his touch. We are without virtue, slag iron, utterly tasteless; uniting (us) with the True Guru, make (us) paaras. All long for heaven, liberation and Baikunth; ever they set hope upon hope (on these). The servants who long for the Lord's sight do not ask for liberation; meeting (him), the mind is filled with the sight and takes comfort. The attachment of Maya is mighty and heavy; attachment stains (the mind) with black stains. The servants of my Master stay untouched and free, as the waterfowl's wings are not wetted (by the water). The fragrance of sandalwood is coiled about by snakes; how is it to be reached, how is the sandalwood to be had? Drawing the keen sword of the Guru's wisdom, cutting and cutting away the poison, the essence is drunk. Wood may be brought and brought and heaped in a great pile; fire turns it to ash in a moment. (So) Saakat men have done most terrible sins; meeting the Saadh, the firebrand is set (to them). The Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones are good, within whom the Naam is set. By (the Name's) touch the holy ones have become paaras (themselves); in them, as it were, the Lord God is seen. The Saakat's thread is full of tangles; how can a warp be woven (from it)? No strand, no thread comes out (of it); keep no company with a Saakat. The Saadh Sangat of the True Guru is good; joining the Sangat, let Ram be remembered. Within are jewels, gems and rubies; they are gained by the Guru's grace. My Master is great, great is my Lord; how can we meet him, how can he be met? O Nanak, the perfect Guru unites (us) in (his) union; (O God,) grant your servant the perfect (state). ॥8॥
The paaras is the stone said to turn iron to gold at its touch; here the paaras is the Guru. Baikunth: in the Puranas, the heaven of Vishnu.
1324.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ram, the all-pervading Ram, Ram alone should be remembered. The Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones are good; meeting the Saadh, let us delight in the Lord's love. All the beings and creatures, as much of the world as there is: (their) mind wavers and wavers. (O God,) show mercy, mercy, and unite (them) with the Saadh (the Guru); give (this) pillar to hold up the world. The earth lies beneath, beneath (all feet), (yet it comes) above all; (so) meeting the Saadh, let us lie in the dust of (his) feet. (Then) you will be most exalted, most exalted; all creation will be laid beneath (your) feet. Through the Guru the good, fair light of Shiv (God) (shines within); (then) Shakti (Maya) comes and fetches water (for that one). Through the Guru's words teeth of wax come forth; chewing and chewing iron (with them), the Lord's essence is drunk. The Guru, the holy Being, has shown great grace with (the gift of) Ram's Name; let us meet him. He has spread abroad the virtues of Ram's Name; the Lord's praise is given out through all the worlds. In the minds of the Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones (dwells) the Beloved; without seeing (him) they cannot live, as the fish of the water loves water, water alone, and without water dies writhing in a moment. Those whose fortune is very bad, very bad, have not drunk the dust of the Saadh's feet. Their craving burns and burns and is never quenched; they are given the punishment of Dharam Raj. Though all pilgrimages, fasts, sacrifices and charities be done, (and) the body be worn away melting and melting in the snow, (still) Ram's Name is a weight beyond weighing, (found) through the Guru's teaching; nothing reaches it, it cannot be weighed on any scale. Your virtues, O Brahm, you alone know, O Brahm; let servant Nanak stay in your refuge. You are the ocean of water, and we are your fish; show mercy and keep (us) with you. ॥8॥
Shiv and Shakti: here Shiv is God, the giver of good, and Shakti is Maya; to fetch water is to serve as a maid.
To chew iron with teeth of wax is a byword for the impossible; here the teeth of wax are a heart made gentle (by the Guru's word), and the iron the mighty vices.
1325.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ram, the all-pervading Ram: let him be worshipped. I would offer up my mind and body and set all before (him); through the Guru's teaching, may the relish (of the Name) and wisdom be made firm (within). The Name of God (Brahm) and (his) virtues are the branches of the tree; picking and picking (their flowers) every day, let worship be done. The Supreme Soul is the god (to worship), and the god is the Supreme Soul; attached to (his) relish, let (him) be worshipped. Discerning understanding is the pure thing in all the world; reflecting and reflecting (with it), let the essence be drunk. By the Guru's grace the treasure (of the Name) has been found; let this mind be given to the True Guru. (The Name) is a priceless, very fine diamond; with (this) diamond let the diamond (of the mind) be pierced. Through the Guru's Shabad the mind becomes an excellent pearl, by which the diamond (of the Name) is assayed. Joining the company of the Sants, (people) are raised high, as the pipal swallows the palas. That mortal becomes the most exalted among all men in whom the fragrance of Ram's Name dwells. (One who) has done many pure, pure deeds: a green branch ever springs forth (on him). Dharam is (its) flower, and the wisdom the Guru has made firm (its) fruit; (its) spreading fragrance is given to the world. The light of the One, the One alone, has come to dwell in the mind; let the vision see the one God in all. The one all-pervading Ram is spread through all; (so) let the head be laid beneath the feet of all. See, without the Name men are noseless (disgraced); their noses are cut, rubbed and rubbed away. Saakat men are called egotists; without the Name, cursed is the living. As long as there is breath, breath in the mind, at once, without delay, take refuge (in him). (O God,) show mercy, mercy, to Nanak, that I may wash the feet of the Saadh. ॥8॥
The pipal and the palas: a pipal that sprouts in a palas tree grows over it and takes it into itself; so the company of the Sants makes a person like them.
1325.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, may I wash the feet of the Saadh, (by which) sins are burnt away in an instant; O my Master, show (this) mercy. (Your) meek beggars stand at (your) door; give the gift to those who long for it so. Save (us), save (us), O God, we have come to (your) refuge; make the Naam firm in me through the Guru's teaching. In the town (of the body) lust and anger are mighty; rising, rising every day, (we) must do battle (with them). Make (us) your own and save (us); through the perfect Guru, draw (us) out. Within is the fire of Maya, fierce and mighty; give (us) the Guru's Shabad, cool as snow, (that) great peace may come to body and mind, the disease be cut away, and (we) may sleep in peace. As the sun with its rays pervades every place, (so) Ram pervades each and every heart. Whoever meets the Saadh, the holy one, gains the relish (of the Name); sitting in one's own home (within), the essence is drunk. The servant (of God) has come to love the Guru as the chakvi (loves) the sight of the sun. Watching and watching, she keeps watch the whole night; (when the sun) shows its face, she drinks Amrit. Saakats are called dogs, very greedy, filled with the filth of much evil-mindedness. For their own ends they talk much; what trust can be placed in them? (O Lord, grant me) the refuge of the Saadh, the holy one, to join the Sangat in which the Lord's essence is drawn out. The (Sants), rich in virtues, speak with their mouths for the good of others; O Lord, grant (me) such Sants and devotees. You are beyond reach, merciful, the Lord of mercy, the Giver; showing mercy to all, save (them). In all beings (you alone are) the one Life of the world; cherish Nanak. ॥8॥
The chakvi (ruddy shelduck), parted from her mate at night, waits all night for the sunrise.
1326.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, make us the servants of (your) servants. As long as there is breath in the mind (and body), let us drink the dust of the Saadh's feet. Shankar (Shiva), Narad, Sheshnag and the sages long for the dust of the Saadh's feet. All the worlds, every one, are made pure where the Saadh sets his feet. Giving up shame (before the world), let all ego be given up; meeting the Saadh, let us stay in (his) company. (He) ends the dread of Dharam Raj, and draws out the one sinking in poison. Those dried up by much doubt, called trees withered where they stand, become green (again) meeting in the Saadh's company. Therefore make no delay, not a moment's delay; go and fall at the feet of the Saadh. The Kirtan of Ram's Name is a jewel, the thing that the Lord has placed with the Saadh. Whoever accepts the Guru's word as true, true, before him (the Saadh) draws it out and sets it. O Sants, hear, hear, O brothers, servants (of God): the Guru, raising his arm, has cried out: if you ever wish for peace, peace for the soul, then take refuge in the True Guru. If (one's) great fortune is very good, then the Naam is made firm (within) through the Guru's teaching. (Then) the whole hard world(-ocean) of attachment to Maya is crossed, (and) in Sahaj the Lord's essence is drunk. Those who are much given to Maya, Maya alone, rot and rot away in Maya. (For them) ignorance is pitch darkness, the road is very hard, (for they) are loaded with the burden of ego. O Nanak, remember, remember Ram, the all-pervading Ram; through Ram (alone) liberation is gained. (When) the True Guru is met, he makes the Naam firm, and (one) blends and merges in Ram's Name.
Narad is a sage of the Puranas, messenger of the gods and a devotee of Vishnu.

1319.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
No one has found the end of Ram, the all-pervading Ram.
(O God,) we are your children, nurtured by you; you are the great Being, my father and my mother.
The Lord's Names are countless and beyond reach; beyond reach, beyond reach is the Lord, the King.
The virtuous and the wise have reflected much, (yet none has) found (his) worth, not even a jot.
(Beings) ever sing the praises of Gobind (the Lord of the universe), of Gobind, but have not found the end of Gobind's praises.
You are beyond measure, beyond weighing, beyond the beyond, O Master; though one repeat (your Name) much, your depth is not found.
Your servants praise you, O Madho; they sing (your) praises, O Lord, O King.
You are the ocean of water, and we are your fish; nowhere has your end been found.
Show mercy to (your) servant, O Madhusudan; O Lord, grant (me) the repeating of the Naam.
For me, a blind fool, the Naam is the prop; servant Nanak has found (it) through the Guru. ॥4॥
1319.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's servant, singing (his) praises, blossoms with joy.
Through the Guru's teaching, devotion to the Lord, Har Har, has come to grace his mind; God wrote (this) on (his) forehead from the very beginning.
Day and night I remember the Guru's feet; in my mind the Lord, Har Har Har, has come to dwell.
In the world the praise of the Lord, Har Har Har, is the excellent thing; as sandalwood rubbed (gives its fragrance, so the Lord's) glory, rubbed (into the heart, spreads its scent).
The Lord's servants have fixed their attention on the Lord, Har Har Har; all the Saakats go after them (in envy).
The slanderer goes his way as his past deeds have ordained; (his) foot touches the she-serpent, and he is burnt (by her venom).
O Lord, my Master, you are the protector of your servants; in every age you have protected your servants.
What came of it that the demon was envious (of the devotee)? Doing all that, he himself withered and fell.
All the beings and creatures that God has made are seized in the mouth of death.
The Lord God, Har Har Har, has protected his servants; servant Nanak has come to his refuge. ॥4॥
1319.3: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, repeat the Name of Jagannath, the Lord of the world.
Whoever has meditated on the Lord's Name through the Guru's teaching, all his sins and sorrows have gone.
(O God,) one tongue cannot sing (your) glory; make (me) with many, many tongues.
Again and again, every moment and every instant, all sing (your) praises, yet they cannot tell your virtues, O God.
Great love has taken hold of me, O God, my Master; I long to see God.
You are the great Giver of all beings; you alone know our pain.
If someone shows (me) the road, the path of God, tell me, what (shall I) give to such a one?
All my body and mind I would offer, dedicate and hand over, if someone who has met God would unite (me with him).
The Lord's virtues are many, many, very many, and great is (his) glory; we can tell only a very little.
Our understanding is in your power, O God, the all-powerful God of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
1320.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, repeat the praises of the Lord, of whom we hear that he is beyond telling.
Dharam, arth, kaam and mokh, all of it follows behind the Lord's servant.
That servant of the Lord meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on whose forehead is great fortune.
Where God asks for the account in his court, there one is set free by having meditated on the Naam.
Our faults of birth after birth are many; pain and the filth of Haumai (ego) cling (to us).
The Guru, showing mercy, bathed (us) in the water of the Lord('s Name), and all sins and wrongs went away.
In the hearts of his servants dwells God the Master; his servants repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Where the last moment comes, there the Naam, (our) companion, protects.
Your servants sing your glory, O Lord, Har Har; O God, Lord of the world, they have repeated (your Name), O Lord.
O God, Master, protector of servant Nanak, save us, sinking like stone. ॥4॥
1320.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord God knows what we think within.
If anyone else slanders the Lord's servant, God does not heed a jot of what he says.
Leaving all else, serve the Imperishable, who is the Master, God, higher than all.
Through serving the Lord, death cannot (so much as) look at (his servant); it comes and falls at the feet of the Lord's servant.
Whomever my Master saves, he gives good counsel, (as if) into his ear.
One whose devotion my God accepts, no one can equal him.
Behold the Lord's wondrous plays, O servant (of God): in the blink of an eye he knows the false from the true.
Therefore his servant is in bliss: the pure in heart meet (him), and the false repent.
O Lord, you are the Giver, the all-powerful Master; O Lord, I beg one gift from you.
O Lord, show mercy and give servant Nanak (this): may your feet, O Lord, ever dwell in my heart. ॥4॥
1321.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O God, treasure of mercy, show mercy, (and) we shall sing the praises of the Lord.
O God, I ever hope in you: when will you take me into your embrace?
We are children, foolish and ignorant; the Father will teach (us) understanding.
The son errs and spoils things moment by moment, (yet the children) will still be dear to the Father of the world.
Whatever you give, O Lord, O Master, that alone shall we receive.
For me there is no other place to which we might go.
The devotees who are dear to the Lord, to them the Lord will be dear.
Merging (their) light in the Light, they will blend into the Light.
The Lord himself, becoming merciful, will himself attune (them) to himself.
Servant Nanak is in (the Lord's) refuge, at (his) door; the Lord will keep (his) honour.
1321.2: Raag Kalyan Bhopali, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Narayan, O Master, you are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), the Supreme God, the remover of pain.
O ocean of peace, O carrier across the world-ocean, O Lord, O Chintamani, all the devotees beg (at your door).
O merciful to the meek, O Lord of the world, O Damodar, O Lord who knows every heart, O Gobind,
O Murari, O Lord Mukand, those who have meditated on Sri Ram through the Guru's teaching have become free of fear.
Those who have sought refuge at the feet of the Lord of the world, those servants have crossed the world-ocean.
The Lord keeps the honour of his devotees; O servant Nanak, the Lord himself shows mercy. ॥2॥
1321.3: Raag Kalyan, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
as the bee (delights) in the nectar (of the flower), may (my) mind delight again and again in (your) lotus feet.
I have no concern with any other water; O Lord, give (this) chatrik the drop (of your Name).
Without meeting (you) there is no contentment; Nanak lives by beholding (your) sight.
Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beggar begs, and begs again, for the Naam alone,
O Support of all, Master of all, Giver of every comfort.
Countless people beg every kind of gift (at your door); whatever the heart longs for, that is received.
Fruitful, fruitful, fruitful is (his) sight, O brother; touching (his feet) again and again, let us sing (his) praises.
O Nanak, (so) the essence merges with the Essence, and the diamond (of the mind) is pierced by the Diamond (of the Lord). ॥2॥
1322.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
that glory is ever new, and dyes the mind (with love).
Brahma, Mahesh, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra beg (of him) the gift of devotion and (his) praise.
Yogis, the wise, those deep in meditation and Sheshnag, all repeat (the Name of) the Lord of countless waves (of wonder).
Says Nanak: I am a sacrifice to the Sants who are ever the companions of God. ॥2॥
1322.2: Raag Kalyan, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Through the love you give, O Lord, Har Har, through (your) love,
with the eyes (you are seen), with speech (you are praised), with the ears (your praise) is heard; in every limb and in the breath there is peace.
Here and there, in all ten directions, he pervades, alike in Mount Meru and in a blade of grass.
Wherever one looks, there the Lord is seen, the Being, the Master (of all), the foremost.
In the Saadh Sangat doubts and fears are wiped away, O Nanak, by speaking the knowledge of God. ॥2॥
1322.3: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God's) praises are (their) naad, the strain of bliss (their) Vedas;
the sages, meeting in the circle of the Sants, speak and hear (them).
(There is) wisdom, meditation, honour and giving; minds that relish (it) repeat the Naam with the tongue, and there sins are destroyed.
Of those who know the way of union, the food of wisdom and the essence of attention on the Shabad, the japa and tapa go on unbroken.
O Nanak, merged with (God's) Light like warp and weft, no pain punishes (them). ॥2॥
1322.4: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
What is the way to him? What shall I do?
(Some) hold to meditation, the knowers of the Shastras to (their) knowledge; (but) how am I to bear this state of mine, which is beyond bearing?
Vishnu, Mahesh, the Siddhas, the sages and Indra: at whose door shall I seek refuge?
With one is a kingdom, with another heaven; (but) among millions, (with whom) can I say liberation is found?
Says Nanak: the relish of the Naam is found if I hold to the feet of the Saadh. ॥2॥
1322.5: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Lord of (my) life, merciful Being, God, (my) friend,
O Lord, destroyer of birth from the womb, of strife, of the net of death and of pain, O protector:
I have held fast to the Naam, (and come) to your refuge;
The helpless and the meek place (their) hope (in you);
the Naam, O Master, is the mantra of (their) minds.
Without you, O God, I know nothing (else);
in every age you are the one I know.
May the Lord dwell in (my) mind night and day;
1322.6: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Let us repeat (the Name of) God with mind and body.
(On whom) the perfect Guru is well pleased, (theirs is) ever peace and bliss.
Singing the praises of Gopal, all tasks have been fulfilled;
(whoever) has remembered God, joining the Saadh Sangat, the pains of death have fled (from him).
O my God, be merciful, so that day and night I may serve (you).
Servant Nanak has come to (your) refuge, O Lord, O Being, O perfect Divine One. ॥2॥
1323.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My God knows every heart; he knows (all).
Show mercy, O perfect Supreme God; (grant me) the unchanging, true Shabad, (the) mark (of entry to your door).
(O God,) apart from the Lord no other is all-powerful; my hope is in you, your strength is in (my) mind.
O Master, Giver to all hearts, what you give, that (we) wear and eat.
Understanding, wisdom, skill, glory, beauty, colour, wealth, honour,
all comforts and bliss (lie in the Naam); O Nanak, repeat the Name of Ram, (it is) every good. ॥2॥
1323.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The refuge of the Lord's feet brings every good;
Whoever repeats (the Naam) without fear in the Saadh Sangat, Jamkaal (death) does not devour him.
Liberation, the ways (to it) and countless comforts do not equal devotion to the Lord.
O servant Nanak, one who longs for the sight of God does not wander into births again. ॥2॥
1323.3: Raag Kalyan, Ashtapadis, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Hearing (the Name of) Ram, the all-pervading Ram, the mind is drenched (with love).
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), a sweet essence; through the Guru's teaching it is drunk in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise).
As fire is in wood, and is drawn out by rubbing it with skill,
(so) the Name of Ram is the light in all (creation); this essence is drawn out through the Guru's teaching.
(The body) has nine doors, and all nine doors are tasteless; the Amrit essence trickles in through the Tenth.
O Beloved, show mercy, mercy, mercy, (that) the Lord's essence may be drunk through the Guru's Shabad.
The body is a town, a fine town; in it let the trade in the Lord's essence be done.
(This essence is) jewels and rubies, priceless, beyond price; they are gained by serving the True Guru.
The True Guru is the Master, beyond reach, beyond reach, a brimming ocean; let devotion (to him) be offered.
(O God,) show mercy, show mercy: we are meek chatriks; put a single drop of the Naam into (our) mouths.
The Beloved is the deep red, red dye; O Guru, give (me this dye) to dye (my) mind.
Those dyed in the love of Ram, Ram, Ram, savouring the essence, drink it ever in deep draughts.
(There is) the earth with its seven continents and the seas; (if they were) dug and the gold drawn out and set (before them),
the servants of my Master would not desire these; they beg for the Lord alone: give (us) the Lord's essence.
Saakat men, mortal beings, are ever hungry; they ever cry hunger, hunger.
Running and racing, they run in the love of Maya, and cover distances of hundreds of thousands of kos.
Exalted are the servants of the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har; what likeness can be given them?
There is no likeness equal to the Name of Ram; (O God,) show mercy to servant Nanak. ॥8॥
1324.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, the Guru is the paaras; grant (me) his touch.
We are without virtue, slag iron, utterly tasteless; uniting (us) with the True Guru, make (us) paaras.
All long for heaven, liberation and Baikunth; ever they set hope upon hope (on these).
The servants who long for the Lord's sight do not ask for liberation; meeting (him), the mind is filled with the sight and takes comfort.
The attachment of Maya is mighty and heavy; attachment stains (the mind) with black stains.
The servants of my Master stay untouched and free, as the waterfowl's wings are not wetted (by the water).
The fragrance of sandalwood is coiled about by snakes; how is it to be reached, how is the sandalwood to be had?
Drawing the keen sword of the Guru's wisdom, cutting and cutting away the poison, the essence is drunk.
Wood may be brought and brought and heaped in a great pile; fire turns it to ash in a moment.
(So) Saakat men have done most terrible sins; meeting the Saadh, the firebrand is set (to them).
The Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones are good, within whom the Naam is set.
By (the Name's) touch the holy ones have become paaras (themselves); in them, as it were, the Lord God is seen.
The Saakat's thread is full of tangles; how can a warp be woven (from it)?
No strand, no thread comes out (of it); keep no company with a Saakat.
The Saadh Sangat of the True Guru is good; joining the Sangat, let Ram be remembered.
Within are jewels, gems and rubies; they are gained by the Guru's grace.
My Master is great, great is my Lord; how can we meet him, how can he be met?
O Nanak, the perfect Guru unites (us) in (his) union; (O God,) grant your servant the perfect (state). ॥8॥
1324.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ram, the all-pervading Ram, Ram alone should be remembered.
The Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones are good; meeting the Saadh, let us delight in the Lord's love.
All the beings and creatures, as much of the world as there is: (their) mind wavers and wavers.
(O God,) show mercy, mercy, and unite (them) with the Saadh (the Guru); give (this) pillar to hold up the world.
The earth lies beneath, beneath (all feet), (yet it comes) above all; (so) meeting the Saadh, let us lie in the dust of (his) feet.
(Then) you will be most exalted, most exalted; all creation will be laid beneath (your) feet.
Through the Guru the good, fair light of Shiv (God) (shines within); (then) Shakti (Maya) comes and fetches water (for that one).
Through the Guru's words teeth of wax come forth; chewing and chewing iron (with them), the Lord's essence is drunk.
The Guru, the holy Being, has shown great grace with (the gift of) Ram's Name; let us meet him.
He has spread abroad the virtues of Ram's Name; the Lord's praise is given out through all the worlds.
In the minds of the Saadhs, the holy, the holy ones (dwells) the Beloved; without seeing (him) they cannot live,
as the fish of the water loves water, water alone, and without water dies writhing in a moment.
Those whose fortune is very bad, very bad, have not drunk the dust of the Saadh's feet.
Their craving burns and burns and is never quenched; they are given the punishment of Dharam Raj.
Though all pilgrimages, fasts, sacrifices and charities be done, (and) the body be worn away melting and melting in the snow,
(still) Ram's Name is a weight beyond weighing, (found) through the Guru's teaching; nothing reaches it, it cannot be weighed on any scale.
Your virtues, O Brahm, you alone know, O Brahm; let servant Nanak stay in your refuge.
You are the ocean of water, and we are your fish; show mercy and keep (us) with you. ॥8॥
1325.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ram, the all-pervading Ram: let him be worshipped.
I would offer up my mind and body and set all before (him); through the Guru's teaching, may the relish (of the Name) and wisdom be made firm (within).
The Name of God (Brahm) and (his) virtues are the branches of the tree; picking and picking (their flowers) every day, let worship be done.
The Supreme Soul is the god (to worship), and the god is the Supreme Soul; attached to (his) relish, let (him) be worshipped.
Discerning understanding is the pure thing in all the world; reflecting and reflecting (with it), let the essence be drunk.
By the Guru's grace the treasure (of the Name) has been found; let this mind be given to the True Guru.
(The Name) is a priceless, very fine diamond; with (this) diamond let the diamond (of the mind) be pierced.
Through the Guru's Shabad the mind becomes an excellent pearl, by which the diamond (of the Name) is assayed.
Joining the company of the Sants, (people) are raised high, as the pipal swallows the palas.
That mortal becomes the most exalted among all men in whom the fragrance of Ram's Name dwells.
(One who) has done many pure, pure deeds: a green branch ever springs forth (on him).
Dharam is (its) flower, and the wisdom the Guru has made firm (its) fruit; (its) spreading fragrance is given to the world.
The light of the One, the One alone, has come to dwell in the mind; let the vision see the one God in all.
The one all-pervading Ram is spread through all; (so) let the head be laid beneath the feet of all.
See, without the Name men are noseless (disgraced); their noses are cut, rubbed and rubbed away.
Saakat men are called egotists; without the Name, cursed is the living.
As long as there is breath, breath in the mind, at once, without delay, take refuge (in him).
(O God,) show mercy, mercy, to Nanak, that I may wash the feet of the Saadh. ॥8॥
1325.2: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, may I wash the feet of the Saadh,
(by which) sins are burnt away in an instant; O my Master, show (this) mercy.
(Your) meek beggars stand at (your) door; give the gift to those who long for it so.
Save (us), save (us), O God, we have come to (your) refuge; make the Naam firm in me through the Guru's teaching.
In the town (of the body) lust and anger are mighty; rising, rising every day, (we) must do battle (with them).
Make (us) your own and save (us); through the perfect Guru, draw (us) out.
Within is the fire of Maya, fierce and mighty; give (us) the Guru's Shabad, cool as snow,
(that) great peace may come to body and mind, the disease be cut away, and (we) may sleep in peace.
As the sun with its rays pervades every place, (so) Ram pervades each and every heart.
Whoever meets the Saadh, the holy one, gains the relish (of the Name); sitting in one's own home (within), the essence is drunk.
The servant (of God) has come to love the Guru as the chakvi (loves) the sight of the sun.
Watching and watching, she keeps watch the whole night; (when the sun) shows its face, she drinks Amrit.
Saakats are called dogs, very greedy, filled with the filth of much evil-mindedness.
For their own ends they talk much; what trust can be placed in them?
(O Lord, grant me) the refuge of the Saadh, the holy one, to join the Sangat in which the Lord's essence is drawn out.
The (Sants), rich in virtues, speak with their mouths for the good of others; O Lord, grant (me) such Sants and devotees.
You are beyond reach, merciful, the Lord of mercy, the Giver; showing mercy to all, save (them).
In all beings (you alone are) the one Life of the world; cherish Nanak. ॥8॥
1326.1: Raag Kalyan, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, make us the servants of (your) servants.
As long as there is breath in the mind (and body), let us drink the dust of the Saadh's feet.
Shankar (Shiva), Narad, Sheshnag and the sages long for the dust of the Saadh's feet.
All the worlds, every one, are made pure where the Saadh sets his feet.
Giving up shame (before the world), let all ego be given up; meeting the Saadh, let us stay in (his) company.
(He) ends the dread of Dharam Raj, and draws out the one sinking in poison.
Those dried up by much doubt, called trees withered where they stand, become green (again) meeting in the Saadh's company.
Therefore make no delay, not a moment's delay; go and fall at the feet of the Saadh.
The Kirtan of Ram's Name is a jewel, the thing that the Lord has placed with the Saadh.
Whoever accepts the Guru's word as true, true, before him (the Saadh) draws it out and sets it.
O Sants, hear, hear, O brothers, servants (of God): the Guru, raising his arm, has cried out:
if you ever wish for peace, peace for the soul, then take refuge in the True Guru.
If (one's) great fortune is very good, then the Naam is made firm (within) through the Guru's teaching.
(Then) the whole hard world(-ocean) of attachment to Maya is crossed, (and) in Sahaj the Lord's essence is drunk.
Those who are much given to Maya, Maya alone, rot and rot away in Maya.
(For them) ignorance is pitch darkness, the road is very hard, (for they) are loaded with the burden of ego.
O Nanak, remember, remember Ram, the all-pervading Ram; through Ram (alone) liberation is gained.
(When) the True Guru is met, he makes the Naam firm, and (one) blends and merges in Ram's Name.
